steps.say: Some prices matter more than others, because of what traders did there. | The chart can show five kinds of them.
We're on Bitcoin, with four-hour candles.
Liquidation levels estimate where leveraged traders would be forced to close. | Red for longs below the price, green for shorts above. Brighter means more money.
Fair value gaps are price ranges a fast move jumped across. | Green ones were left by rises, red ones by falls. | Each stays shaded until price trades back through it.
Single prints, in violet, are prices only one half hour of a day traded through. | Thin areas, which price often comes back to fill.
The anchor tool draws an anchored VWAP. | Tap a candle, such as a swing low, to see the average price paid since then, weighted by volume.
The volume profile tool: drag across a stretch of the chart. | It shows at which prices most trading happened, the busiest price, and the band holding seventy percent of the volume.
None of these is a forecast. | They show where price has reason to pause or turn, so you can plan around them.
